method: The built-in browser pane emulating 360 x 640, the Next.js development server on :3000 against the demonstration API on :8000, dark colour scheme. Every page was loaded, waited for 3.5 s, then checked twice: as it is, and with document.documentElement.style.fontSize = '200%' (the layout's rem units follow the root font). The checker flags: the document wider than 360 px; an element whose box ends outside 360 px (not inside a scroller, not fixed or absolute); a text node whose rendered range ends outside 360 px (this finds text running out of a box that does not grow); an element with text-overflow: ellipsis whose content is longer than it; a box with overflow hidden and content taller than it (a line-clamp is exempt, an sr-only element is exempt). The checker was proved able to fail on a 600 px div, a clipped paragraph and an ellipsis span, and its first version was wrong (it read innerWidth, which grows with the page, so a page that overflowed reported nothing): it uses 360. NOT the sweep and NOT a device.
